idiom_name: typed pipe/compose helpers, or fp-ts flow/pipe
implementation_notes: Function type expressions make each step's contract explicit - `type Fn<A, B> = (a: A) => B` - and functions are values exactly as in JavaScript (TypeScript handbook), so the classic combinator is a typed helper: a fixed-arity generic pipe/compose, or the generated overload ladder that fp-ts ships as `flow` (left-to-right composition, first argument may have any arity) and `pipe` (applies a value through the steps immediately). TypeScript adds no runtime, so no standard-library compose exists; the accurately typed helper or fp-ts replaces the untyped JavaScript idiom, while inline arrows remain appropriate for one-off chains.
pitfalls: A variadic `pipe(...steps)` types as any/unknown after the first step without a large overload set; the accurate typed form is the fixed-arity overload ladder that fp-ts generates.
strictNullChecks propagates through the chain: a step returning T | undefined forces every later step to accept it or the chain stops compiling - correct, but surprising when converting JavaScript.
this-dependent methods lose their receiver type when passed as values; wrap them in an explicit arrow rather than relying on bind.
